_comment: Residuals the quality defence knows about and deliberately still carries.
Unlike .ci/quality-holes.json, whose entries scripts/quality_matrix.py must be able to
derive, these have no measured hole kind: each is a decision or an understood boundary,
so an empty holes registry used to read as 'no blind spots' while the behaviour remained.
Every entry names a live repro: a test carrying @pytest.mark.known_residual(<id>) that
asserts today's behaviour. tests/test_known_residuals.py fails when an entry has no live
repro, when a repro is marked with an unregistered id, and when a marker is malformed.
Fixing a residual reddens the characterization test itself, which forces the entry and
its marker out in the same change.
Fields: id = '<layer>:<name>'; repro = pytest node id of the pinning test; tier = the
layer that owns the fix (rust-core, binding, python-api); opened = date the residual was
registered; exit = the checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must name every id in its Known residuals section.

residuals.exit: to_toml(from_toml('[sec] # note\nx = 1\n')) writes the note on the header line itself; reaching it means changing where the YAML writer places a container's inline note (today: the last line of that container's body) - the placement api:set-comment-container-owner records, not a parser limitation
residuals.why: the note keeps its text and its table but not its line; values are lossless (docs/dev/boundaries.md). The registration blamed granit's capture model; measured 2026-10-25, granit is not in this path, and a YAML-origin `sec: # note` now keeps its line because the TOML section pass reads the key node's inline slot too

residuals.exit: set_comment(..., standalone=False) on a mapping or block sequence keeps the note on the container, at a position the reader reports back from, or refuses the call; the silent handoff to the last child ends
residuals.why: the writer parks a container's inline note on the last child's line, so the re-read gives the note a different owner; the edit fuzz tier withholds the ownership claim (ledger (ei), #113)

residuals.exit: parse('a: 1' + blank + 'b: 2').to_yaml() reproduces the blank at each of the eight positions the repro walks (root, nested key, sequence item, before a note, consecutive, after a block scalar, leading, trailing) instead of emitting the compact form
residuals.why: the reader records no empty line between entries and the writer emits one line break per item, so there is no slot a blank could be restored from; measured 2026-10-27 the edit route drops it too, so no shipped path keeps it. Values, key order, anchors and notes are lossless and the output is already a fixed point, which makes this layout rather than semantics. Filling the slot means per-container writer state, and the Ir gate prices what that costs on the serialize floors (docs/dev/perf.md), so it is registered and declined for now rather than silently absorbed

residuals.exit: parse('port: 8080').validate('type: object\nrequired: [port]\n') either evaluates the YAML spelling or raises pyrs_yaml.YamlValidateError, and the public docstring of Document.validate names the text form the schema argument accepts
residuals.why: the schema parameter is typed `str | dict[str, Any]` and the only text form is JSON: document.rs runs json.loads on the string before the evaluator is consulted, so the spelling a YAML user reaches for comes back as a stdlib json.decoder.JSONDecodeError - outside the ten documented Yaml* classes, and outside the `except YamlValidateError` arm of the CLI, where measured 2026-10-31 `pyrs-yaml validate doc.yaml --schema-file schema.yaml` prints that traceback. Widening acceptance is an interface decision and wrapping the error is an error-contract change; docs/dev/json-schema-engine.md designs the route that makes the question moot

residuals.exit: a named extra installs a JSON Schema evaluator, or Document.validate() refuses with a pyrs_yaml error whose text names the install route, so following docs/en/quick-start.md from its single `pip install pyrs-yaml` line cannot end in a ModuleNotFoundError
residuals.why: Document.validate forwards every rule to `jsonschema` (crates/pyrs-yaml/src/py/document.rs imports it), and no distribution this project publishes installs that package: [project.dependencies] is typing-extensions alone and the three extras are cli, pydantic and settings, while jsonschema sits in the test group. Measured 2026-10-31 with the module halted in sys.modules - the same failure an absent wheel gives - the call raises a bare ModuleNotFoundError that names nothing the reader can act on. An extra is a packaging decision (AGENTS.md: ask first), and the evaluator this repository owns is the design under review in docs/dev/json-schema-engine.md
